match.reason: None of the bank points explains that volcanoes form where plates pull apart or one slides under another; they cover volcanic hazards, how volcanism builds landforms, and mountain building from plates pushing together.

draft.title: What causes volcanic eruptions
card: Magma is molten rock beneath the Earth's surface. It is hot and lighter than the solid rock around it, so it can rise.
Magma often rises where two plates pull apart. The gap lets magma move up from below.
Magma also rises where one plate slides under another. The plate that sinks melts, and the new magma rises through the plate above.
A volcanic eruption happens when magma reaches the surface. It comes out as lava (molten rock on the surface), ash and gas.
draft.remember: Magma rises where plates pull apart or one slides under another, then erupts as lava, ash and gas.

a.q: What is an eruption of a volcano?
opts: Magma reaching the surface as lava, ash and gas
Solid rock sliding down a steep slope after rain
Plates suddenly slipping and shaking the ground
Water rising from the sea floor as a huge wave
a.why: An eruption happens when magma reaches the surface and comes out as lava, ash and gas. Rock sliding down a slope is a different event, and so is the sudden slipping of plates.
a.clue: Think about what comes out of the ground.

b.q: Near a coast, one plate slides under another. Why might a volcano form on the plate above?
opts: The sinking plate melts and the new magma rises
The sinking plate pushes solid rock up as lava
The plates pull apart and sea water floods in
The plate above melts because it is lighter
b.why: The plate that sinks melts, and the new magma rises through the plate above. The magma, not solid rock, is what erupts. The plate above is not the one that melts.
b.clue: Which plate goes down, and what happens to it?

wants.brief: A cross-section of one plate sliding under another. Label: plate sliding under, plate above, magma rising, volcano erupting with lava, ash and gas.
wants.why: It shows how a sinking plate leads to magma rising to a volcano.

a.best: Magma reaching the surface as lava, ash and gas

b.best: The sinking plate melts and the new magma rises

problems.detail: The card and why (b) say the sinking plate itself melts, and why (b) adds that 'the plate above is not the one that melts'. In current science, water released from the sinking plate mostly melts the mantle wedge above it, and the base of the overriding plate can melt too. 'The sinking plate melts' is a common school simplification, but stating flatly that the plate above does not melt is misleading. Consider wording like 'water from the sinking plate helps rock above it melt, and this magma rises'.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear answer that matches the card. However, the card and why (b) oversimplify subduction melting: in reality, water from the sinking plate mostly melts the mantle above it, and why (b) wrongly denies that the upper plate melts.
